1.why: All nine screens are static single-card forms with no animations, moving images, or pop-up elements visible.

2.why: Bold headings, teal primary buttons, and bordered callouts make key items stand out, although the dark Logs panel visually competes with the main card.

3.why: Each screen shows only one labeled input and at most three buttons, so the needed control is quick to locate.

4.why: Password rules and codes are displayed at the point of use and each screen directs the next action, so little must be remembered beyond the newly created password.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, or password-manager option appears on any screen, and the sign-in page lacks even a username field.

6.why: The typed email and the pre-filled recovery code can be recognized, but no saved or remembered items such as a remembered identifier are ever shown.

7.why: Sentences are short and plainly worded, though terms like 'recovery identifier,' 'MFA code,' and 'simulated secure authenticator' assume some technical familiarity.

8.why: No error state or error message appears in any of the nine screenshots, so there is no evidence that errors describe the problem and how to fix it.

9.why: No example inputs or placeholders are provided; requirements are abstract ('at least 12 characters, including uppercase and lowercase letters, a number, and a symbol') with no sample value shown.

10.why: The system enforces a fixed password-then-MFA path and never offers alternative authentication choices such as face login, so no such clear choices exist.

11.why: No screen presents more than three buttons and usually a single primary action, keeping simultaneous choices low.

12.why: Every action yields visible feedback via an inline confirmation line and a Logs entry, though the log wording is technical ('Simulated ... completed.').

13.why: Each step includes a brief instruction line and a safety-tip callout, e.g., 'Use the secure link you received or enter the delivered recovery code manually.'

14.why: 'Start over,' 'Forgot password?,' and the persistent resend button allow restarting, but no error-and-retry screen is shown to demonstrate easy recovery from a mistake.

15.why: All screens reuse the same header, card layout, teal/gray button styles, callouts, and Logs panel, making the design consistent and learnable over time.
